assertions: Java source compiles using only the official COMSOL client classpath and external JDK 11.
Worker binds a loopback ephemeral port and rejects an incorrect token.
A nonblocking request receives an original request_id, remains queryable to terminal failure, and health remains responsive.
Persistent endpoint metadata contains a 0600 reconnect token, while the token is passed to Java through the child environment rather than its command line.
A new control wrapper reattaches the live Worker endpoint without spawning a replacement or killing the original child.
A confirmed-dead private Worker endpoint starts the replacement at a higher generation, invalidating old opaque handles.
Reusing a request_id with a different request body is rejected without replay; unknown internal commands are rejected; concurrent health calls remain responsive.
Operation-context request events preserve operation/request linkage while redacting password fields, and nested map/array result encoding stays structured rather than becoming a Java handle.
Implicit current-file saves and explicit saves use the same atomic publisher; arbitrary paths outside the configured project root are rejected before the raw COMSOL save callback.
Worker generation changes are synchronized to the private reconnect record, and runtime metadata exposes an instance identifier without exposing its token.
Two independent persistent Java Workers competing for the same synthetic endpoint lock produce ENGINE_BUSY for the second Worker without any COMSOL connection.

engine_scope: No ModelUtil.connect, model load/create/save, solve, or existing COMSOL server action was executed by this control-plane test.
limitations: This is not real COMSOL engine acceptance for T012/T026/T028/T055.
Live ModelChangedHandler delivery, revision fingerprinting, and Worker-to-MCP integration remain pending dependency-gated W05/W06 tests.
Windows, macOS Intel, COMSOL 6.3, and GUI Desktop remain UNVERIFIED.
